title: SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA

sections.title: Solution Architecture
sections.text:
9.1 Solution Architecture
Let’s get started with an overview of SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for
SAP S/4HANA. The following solutions are offered in SAP Digital Supply Chain Manage-
ment, edition for SAP S/4HANA:
 Enterprise portfolio and project management
 Extended warehouse management
 Transportation management
 Yard logistics
 Extended service parts planning
 Manufacturing for planning and scheduling
 Production engineering and operations

9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
548
These solutions are also offered as embedded options in SAP S/4HANA. But for compa-
nies who still leverage the SAP ERP system as their core ERP system and want to use
these capabilities, SAP Digital Supply Chain Management is an option to deploy it side
by side along with the SAP ERP system. In addition, multiple ERP systems can be con-
nected to one SAP Digital Supply Chain system depending on the capability being lev-
eraged, which simplifies the overall solution landscape.
For companies that are already on SAP S/4HANA but want to leverage the new SAP Dig-
ital Supply Chain capabilities that aren’t yet available in their SAP S/4HANA release, the
SAP Digital Supply Chain system is an option to deploy a sidecar system with a higher
SAP S/4HANA release to leverage the latest innovations in these solutions. Frequent
upgrades can be performed in the sidecar SAP Digital Supply Chain systems, so that the
latest features and functionalities introduced in SAP S/4HANA can be consumed for
the available capabilities in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. The modularity of the
solutions usually brings in speed of consuming innovations in SAP solutions and flex-
ibility in terms of changes to be introduced in the solution landscape.
As shown in Figure 9.1, core ERP processes such as production planning and control or
sales and distribution are executed in the core ERP system, and the advanced features
are executed in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. Standard integration options are
available between the ERP and SAP Digital Supply Chain components.

9.1 Solution Architecture
Within SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, the SAP
S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling solution is the focus of this chap-
ter. SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling is another SAP S/4HANA
system, but it only runs the embedded PP/DS solution. It can integrate to one or more
SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA systems (core ERP) and integrate with components such as
materials management for external procurement, production planning for manufac-
turing, plant maintenance for resource downtimes and materials reservations, quality
management for inspection lots, sales and distribution for sales orders, and so on.
In SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling, the following scenarios
are supported:
 Discrete manufacturing
 Process manufacturing
 Repetitive manufacturing
 Make-to-order (MTO)
 Make-to-stock (MTS)
 Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP)
 Engineer-to-order (ETO), including variant configuration (VC)
We’ll refer to the core ERP system—SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA—as the ERP system, and
SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling as the planning and schedul-
ing system, in this chapter.
The technical architecture of the planning and scheduling system is shown in Figure
9.2. The ERP system is the master system for all the master data objects, such as mate-
rial master, resource/work center master, BOMs/routings and production versions,
master recipes, location master data such as plants/material requirements planning
(MRP) areas/business partners, and external procurement master data such as pur-
chasing info records/contracts/scheduling agreements.
The master data objects are integrated from the ERP system to the planning and sched-
uling system via the core interface leveraging integration models. There are certain
master data objects that can’t be transferred to the planning and scheduling system via
the core interface and need to be maintained manually, such as the location master
data. We’ll cover the details in Section 9.4.1.
The transaction data objects, including procurement proposals (planned orders, pur-
chase requisitions), purchase orders, process/production orders, sales orders, and
inventory/batches, are also integrated via the core interface and the corresponding
integration models.
The planning and scheduling system will have SAP liveCache in its SAP HANA database
for PP/DS functionalities. In addition, the optimizer engine for the Production Plan-
ning Optimizer and Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is also connected to the planning
and scheduling system.

9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
550
Figure 9.2 Architecture of SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling
Connected to the ERP System
For the SAP Fiori apps offered in the ERP system and in the planning and scheduling
system, one SAP Gateway system, which is connected to both the ERP and planning and
scheduling systems, can be in the landscape to support both systems.
From the planning and scheduling functionalities perspective, all the chapters we’ve
covered earlier for PP/DS are still applicable, except for any specific functionalities that
are part of the restrictions list for the planning and scheduling solution.
Following are the usage restrictions for the planning and schedulingsystem:
 Available-to-promise (ATP) or advanced ATP (aATP) checks in the connected ERP sys-
tem for planned orders, production orders, and process orders can’t be triggered
from the planning and scheduling system. However, the order availability checks
can be performed within the ERP system.
 For executing planning runs, for materials integrated to the planning and schedul-
ing system for PP/DS planning, the planning runs must be performed within the
planning and scheduling system using the PP/DS planning run (Transaction
/SAPAPO/CDPSB0). MRP Live in the ERP system can only plan the non-PP/DS mate-
rials (materials that aren’t integrated to the planning and scheduling system, a cor-
responding MRP type assigned in the material master such as PD, etc.).
 Use of reference capacities in resource/work center master data isn’t supported as of
SAP S/4HANA release 2022 for the planning and scheduling system.
 Usage and integration of article master data, which is used in retail industry scenar-
ios, isn’t supported.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.text:
9.2 Prerequisites
 If the ERP system is an SAP ERP system, then the discrete industry and mill products
(DIMP) business function called LAMA (activation of long material number) can’t be
active in the ERP system.
 Master data objects, such as plants/MRP areas, business partners, penalties for the
Production Planning Optimizer maintained in the material master and work center
master, and the time-dependent safety stock levels maintained in the ERP system
can’t be transferred via core interface. These objects should be created and main-
tained manually in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system.
9.2 Prerequisites
For connecting an ERP system to the planning and scheduling system, there are certain
software release-level restrictions. Only systems that are compatible with the release
version can be connected, as shown in Table 9.1.
Tip
Many of the setup steps for configuring the ERP and SAP Digital Supply Chain systems
are already covered in Chapter 3, so we won’t repeat such details in this chapter.
Other prerequisites include the following:

database, and the SAP liveCache connections are set up.

sections.title: Customizing and Configuration
sections.text:
9.3 Customizing and Configuration
In this section, we’ll cover the configuration settings required in the ERP system and in
the planning and scheduling system for the integration of data. In addition, within the
planning and scheduling system, we’ll also cover the PP/DS customization settings.

sections.title: Settings in the ERP System
sections.text:
9.3.1 Settings in the ERP System
In this section, we’ll cover the customizing settings that need to be maintained in the
ERP system.
Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape
The following basic settings for setting up the landscape are available under Customiz-
ing menu path SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and
Optimization  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape:
 Name logical system
 Assign logical system to client
 Specify the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization release
In the Customizing node, as shown in Figure 9.3, enter the logical system (Log.System)
as the logical system ID for the SAP Digital Supply Chain system: “DSCCLNT001”, in the
system type (Syst.Type) field, enter “SAP_S4HANA”, and in the Release field, enter the
SAP S/4HANA release of the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. In our example, the SAP
Digital Supply Chain system is an SAP S/4HANA 2022 system, so the release is main-
tained as “107”.
Figure 9.3 Specify the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization
Release for SAP Digital Supply Chain System’s Logical System
© 

553
9.3 Customizing and Configuration
The next step is to set up the RFC destination. Follow SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Inte-
gration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimization  Basic Set-
tings for Setting Up the System Landscape  Set Up RFC Destination. The RFC destination
must be created with the same name as the logical system defined for the SAP Digital
Supply Chain system.
After the RFC destination is created, assign the RFC destination to the application. Nav-
igate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced
Planning and Optimization  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape 
Assign RFC Destinations to Different Application Cases. In this Customizing node, make
a new entry, and, as shown in Figure 9.4, enter the SAP Digital Supply Chain system’s
logical system in the Log.System field. Leave the application (Appl.) field with a blank
value, and assign the RFC destination created for the SAP Digital Supply Chain system
in the RFC Destination field.
Figure 9.4 Assign the RFC Destination to Applications for the SAP Digital Supply Chain System
The next step is to set the target system and the queue type. Navigate to SAP IMG menu
path, SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimi-
zation  Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape  Set Target System and
Queue Type. In this Customizing transaction, make a new entry, and maintain the SAP
Digital Supply Chain system’s logical system as the Log.System and maintain the
Queue Type with value I (inbound queue).
Basic Settings for Data Transfer
The basic settings for setting up the landscape are available under Customizing menu
path SPRO  Integration with Other SAP Components  Advanced Planning and Optimi-
zation  Basic Settings for the Data Transfer. In the Configure Change Transfer for Mas-
ter Data Customizing node or using Transaction CFC9, make the settings shown in
Figure 9.5 for the change transfer of the master data objects.
Under the Change Transfer for Master data area 1, use value 2 (BTE Transfer, Immedi-
ately) for the Material Master Change Transfer, maintain a blank value (No Change

9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
554
Transfer) for the Change Transfer for Customers and Change Transfer for Vendors fields,
maintain the value 2 (BTE Transfer, Immediately) for Change Transfer for Setup Groups.
Figure 9.5 Change Transfer Settings for Master Data in the ERP System
Under Initial Data Transfer and Change Transfer for Resource, select the Immediate
Transfer checkbox to enable the immediate transfer of changes made to the ERP
resource/work center master data. Maintain a blank entry for Use Ext. Capacity (use
external capacity), and for the Change Transf. Mode, maintain value A (Chng Trans. for
Pl.-Vers-Indep. Res. and all PVs Model 000).
The other settings available in this Customizing transaction (see Figure 9.5 2) are rele-
vant in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system and not in the ERP system:
© 

555
9.3 Customizing and Configuration
 Activation of Application Link Enabling (ALE) change pointers for message types
In Transaction BD50, make sure that the change pointers are activated for the mes-
sage type CIFSRC.
 Activation of online transfer using business transfer events (BTEs)
In Transaction BF11M, make sure the business transfer events New Dimension
Plugin APO (ND-APO) and New Dimension Integration (NDI) are activated.
 Register the RFC destination and register queue names
For the outbound transfer of data from the ERP system to the planning and schedul-
ing system, use Transaction SMQS to register the RFC destination. For processing
inbound queues from the planning and scheduling system to the ERP system, regis-
ter the CF* queue using Transaction SMQR in the ERP system.

sections.title: Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling
sections.text:
9.3.2 Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling
Like the ERP system, in the planning and scheduling system as well the core interface,
settings need to be maintained for processing master data and transaction data sent
from the ERP system. In addition, settings are needed to integrate the planning and
scheduling results in terms of procurement proposals, such as planned order and pur-
chase requisitions, back to the ERP system. We’ll discuss the key settings required in
the planning and scheduling system in the following sections.
Basic Settings for Setting Up the System Landscape
In the planning and scheduling system, the core interface settings are maintained in
SAP IMG Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Integration via Core
Interface (CIF). Under the basic settings for creating the system landscape, perform the
following steps to define the basic settings for the core interface:
 Name logical systems.
 Assign the logical system to the client.
 Set up the RFC destination (from the planning and scheduling system to the ERP sys-
tem).
 Assign RFC destinations to various application cases.
In the Customizing node Assign RFC Destinations to various application cases, under
the preceding SAP IMG menu path, assign an RFC Destination to the ERP system cre-
ated with a dialog user assigned to it to the applications shown in Figure 9.6. In the CIF
Applicatn (core interface application) column, select Display Application Log of another
system to enable the selection and display of the application logs from the ERP systems
in the planning and scheduling system in the core interface postprocessing transaction
(Transaction /SAPAPO/CPP). Select Order Navigation from the same column to enable
the navigation to transactions in the ERP system to display the order details from the

9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
556
planning and scheduling system transactions, such as the product view (Transaction
/SAPAPO/RRP3).
Figure 9.6 Assigning RFC Destinations for Core Interface Applications in
SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling
Maintain Business System Group is an important Customizing setting. As multiple ERP
systems can be connected to the planning and scheduling system, the business system
group is the setting that differentiates the data coming in from different ERP systems
into the planning and scheduling system. In the initial screen of this Customizing
transaction, click on the New Entries button to create new entries for the business sys-
tem group for all the ERP systems to be connected to the planning and scheduling sys-
tem, as shown in Figure 9.7.
Figure 9.7 Maintaining Business System Groups in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning
and Scheduling
In the next step, we link the logical systems (ERP systems) to the corresponding busi-
ness system group created in the steps. Navigate to SAP IMG menu path SPRO 
Advanced Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Integration  Basic Settings for
Creating the System Landscape  Assign Logical System and Queue Type. In this transac-
tion, as shown in Figure 9.8, maintain the business system group in the BusSystGrp
field, and maintain the Logical system for the connected ERP systems. Set the value “X”
for the SAP Ind. field, along with the Rel field with value “700”. In the Queue Type, select
the Inbound Queues, and activate Postprocessing in the Err. Hndlg field.
© 

557
9.3 Customizing and Configuration
Figure 9.8 Assignment of Logical System and Queue Type in SAP S/4HANA
Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling
Next, register inbound queues using Transaction SMQR for processing inbound queues
from the ERP systems. In addition, register the RFC destination for the outbound pro-
cessing of data from SAP Digital Supply Chain to the ERP system using Transaction
SMQS. Refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.2, for the details.
In Transaction CFC9 settings in SAP Digital Supply Chain, make the same settings as
mentioned in Section 9.3.1. In addition, you can also make the settings per specific
requirements shown previously in Figure 9.5 1. In the SAP Digital Supply Chain sys-
tem, you also activate the change pointers for message type CIFSRC in Transaction
BD50. Then, using Transaction BF11, activate online transfer using BTEs for the NDI and
ND-APO applications.
Maintain distribution definitions under Customizing menu path, SPRO  Advanced
Planning  Integration via Core Interface (CIF)  Basic Settings for Data Transfer  Publi-
cation  Maintain Distribution Definition. In this transaction, make new entries for the
External Procurement and In-House Production order objects for all the locations
(plants and MRP areas; in our example, location PPS5), and enter the logical system of
the connected ERP system in the LogSystem column, as shown in Figure 9.9.
Figure 9.9 Creation of Distribution Definitions in
SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling

9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
558
This distribution definition determines the destination of the connected ERP system
for the transactional data objects created and changed in the planning and scheduling
system. This step must be performed after the PP/DS locations are created in the plan-
ning and scheduling system, as described in Section 9.3.2.
The last step is to maintain the retransfer settings for the in-house production orders
under SAP IMG Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Integration via
Core Interface (CIF)  Basic Settings for Data Transfer  Publication  Maintain Object-
Specific Settings. In this transaction, create a new entry, select In-House Production in
the Publ. Type (publication type) column, and select Always Retransfer in the Retrans-
fer column, as shown in Figure 9.10. When orders are changed in the ERP system, the
order is transferred to the planning and scheduling system via the core interface. If the
order has to be changed in the planning and scheduling system when the core interface
is updating (e.g., resource downtimes cause the order dates to be changed in the plan-
ning and scheduling system), the retransfer settings make sure the new date for the
orders is also immediately sent back to the ERP system.
Figure 9.10 Retransfer Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling
Global Settings
Activate advanced planning in the planning and scheduling system using SAP IMG
menu path SPRO  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Activate Advanced Planning and
Scheduling  Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling. In this Customizing transac-
tion, select the Activate Advanced Planning and Scheduling checkbox, and save the
transaction.
Next, you need to set up the data transfer. Under SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Advanced
Planning  Basic Settings  Settings for Data Transfer, as shown in Figure 9.11, deselect all
the transaction data objects. As the transfer of the transaction data is initiated in the
ERP system via the core interface, the data transfer settings within the planning and
scheduling system aren’t relevant.
© 

559
9.3 Customizing and Configuration
Figure 9.11 Data Transfer Settings in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for
Planning and Scheduling
The following steps are the basic PP/DS settings for the planning and scheduling sys-
tem (refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.2, for details of these steps):
1. Define the configuration schema (CDP or VC).
2. Maintain the number ranges for orders in PP/DS.
3. Assign the number range for the orders in the PP/DS global settings and defaults
(Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1).
4. For forecast and sales order consumption, maintain the corresponding settings for
category groups and check mode.
5. When CDP functionalities are used in the planning and scheduling system, includ-
ing shelf-life planning, maintain organizational areas for class type 023 under the
object MARA. The organizational areas must be created with the same values as the
organizational areas defined in the ERP system.
6. Create the active model (000) and active planning version (000) in the planning and
scheduling system using Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM.
The following steps are ERP Customizing for basic master data elements such as MRP
controllers and person responsible for the work centers. We won’t cover these steps in
detail as these are basic ERP customizations for SAP S/4HANA production planning.
1. Define the person responsible under the Customizing menu path SPRO  Advanced
Planning  Master Data  Specify Person Responsible (Planner). In the planning and
scheduling system, create the person responsible with the same names as that of the
MRP controllers defined in the connected ERP systems. In the planning and schedul-
ing and embedded PP/DS systems, the person responsible isn’t connected to the

9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
560
location (plants or MRP areas). So, in the ERP system, define the MRP controllers in a
way that they are unique values for different plants.
2. In the SAP Digital Supply Chain system, define the MRP groups and MRP controllers
the same as in the connected ERP systems.
3. Define the special procurement keys and the plant-level maintenance of the special
procurement settings in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system. Define the special pro-
curement keys with the same name as defined in the ERP systems.
4. For the work centers, in the SAP Digital Supply Chain system, define the person
responsible for the work centers under the ERP work center customization settings.
In addition, if shift data is leveraged in the ERP system, define the corresponding
shifts and related Customizing data in the planning and scheduling system. The
work center formulas need to be created in the planning and scheduling system the
same as the formulas defined in the ERP system.
Material Master Settings
In the planning and scheduling system, when material masters are transferred from
the ERP system via the core interface integration model, it creates the material master
first. This material master is made available to PP/DS in the planning and scheduling
system by an automatic activation of the Advanced Planning indicator in the material
master. Therefore, it’s important that the following Customizing settings in the plan-
ning and scheduling system for the material master are maintained:
 Field selection
In SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Logistics – General  Material Master  Field Selection 
Maintain Field Selection for Data Screens, compare the settings between the plan-
ning and scheduling system and the ERP system. The fields marked as required entry
(Reqd Entry), as shown in Figure 9.12, in the planning and scheduling system, should
also be set as required entry in the ERP system. When certain fields are marked as
mandatory fields in the planning and scheduling system, if those fields aren’t filled
in for the ERP system (because they are set as optional fields in the ERP system), the
transfer of material master from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling sys-
tem will fail. So, for other fields in the planning and scheduling system that are rele-
vant views in the material master (e.g., the MRP views), for the fields that are relevant
in the ERP system (e.g., scrap-related fields, stock determination, etc.), mark them as
optional fields in both systems so that the core interface transfer of the materials
doesn’t fail in the inbound queues in the planning and scheduling system.
 Quantity/value update and material types
In the planning and scheduling system, the material master is created for facilitating
the advanced planning, and the planning and scheduling system isn’t the system of
record for inventory and its valuation. So, in SAP IMG menu path SPRO  Logistics –
General  Material Master Basic Settings Material Types Define Attributes of Mate-
rial Types, in the planning and scheduling system, deselect the Value updating
checkboxes for all material types and valuation areas, as shown in Figure 9.13.
© 

561
9.3 Customizing and Configuration
Figure 9.12 Material Master Field Selection in ERP and SAP S/4HANA
Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling Systems
Figure 9.13 Deselecting Value Updating for Material Types in SAP S/4HANA
Manufacturing for Planning and Scheduling

9 SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA
562
Apart from the Value updating, other settings ensure the material type details settings
are the same in the planning and scheduling and ERP systems. In addition, ensure that
the definition of key fields under Customizing menu path SPRO  Logistics – General 
Material Master  Settings for Key Fields, are maintained the same in the ERP and plan-
ning and scheduling systems.

sections.title: Integration
sections.text:
9.4 Integration
The master data and the transaction data from the connected ERP system needs to be
integrated to the planning and scheduling system for performing the planning and
scheduling activities in the planning and scheduling system. In this section we will
cover the details of the integration of master data and the transaction data objects.

sections.title: Integration of Master Data
sections.text:
9.4.1 Integration of Master Data
Except for the location master data, all other master data is transferred from the ERP
system to the planning and scheduling system via the core interface integration
model. The details of creating and activating the integration model are already covered
in Chapter 3. In this section, we’ll focus specifically on relevant master data for SAP Dig-
ital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA.
Location Master Data
The ERP plant, MRP areas, and business partners are required in the planning and
scheduling system as the location master data. Transferring the material master from
the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system first creates the material master
in the planning and scheduling system and then activates the Advanced Planning indi-
cator in an automatic way. So, to enable the creation of the material master in the plan-
ning and scheduling system, the plant and MRP areas also need to be defined in the
planning and scheduling system.
The plant data needs to be assigned with the factory calendar in the planning and
scheduling system, so before creating the plants in the planning and scheduling sys-
tem, create the factory calendars the same as the factory calendars in the ERP systems.
To create the plant in the planning and scheduling system, navigate to Customizing
menu path SPRO  Enterprise Structure  Definition  Logistics – General  Define Copy
Delete Check Plant  Define Plant. Here, create a new entry for all the plants correspond-
ing to the plants defined in the connected ERP systems.
Once the plant is created, assign the plant to a company code using SAP IMG menu path
SPRO  Enterprise Structure  Assignment  Logistics – General  Assign Plant to Company
Code. As the planning and scheduling system isn’t relevant for any financial or con-
trolling processes, the company code in the planning and scheduling system can be
© 

563
9.4 Integration
defined independently with only the mandatory fields, and the company codes need
not match the ERP systems.
The MRP area is another location master data item that needs to be defined in the plan-
ning and scheduling system. As MRP areas will be assigned with storage locations or
subcontracting vendors (business partners), create the corresponding storage loca-
tions and the business partners in the planning and scheduling system. To create the
MRP areas in the planning and scheduling system, follow SAP IMG menu path SPRO 
Production  Material Requirement Planning  Master Data  MRP Areas  Define MRP
Areas for Plants/Storage Locations or Define MRP Areas for Subcontractors.
If the externally procured materials are also planned in the planning and scheduling
system, it’s required to have the location master data representing the vendors (busi-
ness partners) available in the planning and scheduling system. As the core interface
integration model–based transfer for business partners isn’t supported in the planning
and scheduling system, it’s required to create the business partners manually in the
planning and scheduling system using Transaction BUP1. As the vendor business part-
ner is only relevant in the planning and scheduling system to assign the vendor loca-
tion to purchase requisitions during planning, it’s sufficient only to maintain the
mandatory fields in the basic and purchasing organization views.
Tip
If the customer/vendor integration (CVI) is defined in the ERP systems, the ALE (IDocs)
or Data Replication Framework (DRF) can be used to replicate the business partner data
from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system.
Once all the required basic location master data items (e.g., plants, MRP areas, and busi-
ness partners) are defined, execute program /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION in the plan-
ning and scheduling system to create the PP/DS locations in the planning and
scheduling system. The steps and data flow are shown in Figure 9.14.

Other Master Data
For other material master data objects, such as the material master, resource/work cen-
ter master, BOMs/routings/production versions, master recipes, and external procure-
ment master data (purchasing info records, contracts, scheduling agreements), create
an integration model in the ERP system using Transaction CFM1, and activate the inte-
gration model to transfer the data to the planning and scheduling system.
Warning
In the ERP system, don’t activate the Advanced Planning indicator in the Advanced
Planning view of the material master for the materials that are integrated to the plan-
ning and scheduling system. If the Advanced Planning indicator is selected in the SAP
S/4HANA (ERP) system, it will be integrated to embedded PP/DS of the same SAP
S/4HANA system. If you also integrate the material to the planning and scheduling sys-
tem via the core interface integration model, this will lead to data inconsistencies in
the system.
After the activation of the integration model, the material master is available and the
Advanced Planning flag is activated via a standard delivered enhancement (BAdI) CIF_
S4_BADI_PRODUCT_OUTBOUND in the planning and scheduling system. Within the planning
and scheduling system, you can maintain PP/DS-specific fields such as product heuris-
tics, safety stock settings, and so on. In addition, you can leverage the just-mentioned
BAdI to also fill any other additional attributes of the material master with respect to
the PP/DS-related fields.
For the work centers and resources, the integration model activation will create the
work center and resources in the planning and scheduling system, and the standard
delivered enhancement BAdI CIF_S4_WORK_CENTER_OUTBOUND will set the Advanced Plan-
ning indicator within the SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling
system, which in turn creates the PP/DS resource master.
For the in-house manufacturing master data, such as BOMs/routings/production ver-
sions and master recipes, the creation and activation of integration models will create
the production data structures (PDSs) in the planning and scheduling system. The
BOMs/routings/production versions and master recipes aren’t replicated as the same
objects in the planning and scheduling system; instead, the PDS is directly generated.
Similarly for the external procurement master data, such as the purchasing info
records, contracts, and scheduling agreements, the external procurement relation-
ships are directly generated in the planning and scheduling system.
For the classification data, such as classes and characteristics, you need to create an
integration model in the ERP system with the filters for the organizational area
assigned to the classes and characteristics and also apply filters for specific characteris-
tics you want to transfer to the planning and scheduling system. Upon activation of the

9.4 Integration
integration model, the class and characteristics are available in the planning and sched-
uling system. In addition, another integration needs to be created within the planning
and scheduling system with the same filters applied in the ERP system. Upon activa-
tion of the integration model within the planning and scheduling system, the classes
and characteristics are available for PP/DS.
Note
Only the integration of class types 001, 023, and 300 are supported via the core inter-
face integration from the ERP system to the planning and scheduling system.
For maintenance of Production Planning Optimizer–specific penalties, use Transaction
/SAPAPO/PPO_DPEN in the planning and scheduling system to maintain the penalty
values. For time-dependent penalties and time-dependent safety stocks, use Transac-
tion /SAPAPO/TDS in the planning and scheduling system.

9.4.2 Integration of Transaction Data
The integration of the transaction data between the ERP system and the planning and
scheduling system is performed via the core interface using the integration models. In
the ERP system, create the integration models for all the transaction data objects such
as planned independent requirements (PIRs), sales orders, reservations, purchase
orders, purchase requisitions, planned orders, production/process orders, stocks,

batches, and so on. Activation of the integration models will send the data from the ERP
system to the planning and scheduling system. Once the integration model is active,
any changes made in the data in the ERP side will flow to the planning and scheduling
system and vice versa via the core interface queues.
For transaction data such as sales orders, PIRs, material reservations, stocks, and batches,
the ERP system is the master system, and such data only flows from the ERP system to
the planning and scheduling system. For purchase orders/requisitions and the produc-
tion/planned order objects, these can be changed in both systems, and core interface
transfers will be triggered as soon as the changes are saved in either of the systems.
Note
The administrative tools explained in Chapter 10 are applicable to the planning and
scheduling system as well. The housekeeping/consistency check jobs with respect to
the embedded PP/DS should be executed in the planning and scheduling system, and
the jobs relevant for the SAP S/4HANA system should be executed in the ERP systems.
For the correctness of the planning results, you need to ensure that a component at any
BOM level is integrated to the planning and scheduling system for advanced planning,
and all the components, semifinished products, and finished products above the com-
ponent are also planned in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling.
For the planning and scheduling materials in the ERP system, the MRP type will be set
as X0 - W/O MRP, with BOM explosion. So, such materials won’t be planned during the
MRP Live or classic MRP planning in the ERP system.
For example, component C1 (MRP type X0) is planned in the planning and scheduling
system, the semifinished product S1 isn’t planned in SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for
planning and scheduling (MRP type PD), and the finished product F1 is planned in the
planning and scheduling system (MRP type X0). During the planning run in the plan-
ning and scheduling system, because the S1 material isn’t in the system, it doesn’t gen-
erate a dependent demand for S1 in the planning and scheduling system. When the
planned order for F1 is integrated back to the ERP system, in the next MRP planning in
the ERP system, the planned order for F1 is re-exploded, the dependent demand is cre-
ated, and a planned order is also created in the ERP system. Because S1 isn’t in the plan-
ning and scheduling system, the planned order isn’t sent to the planning and
scheduling system, so component C1 won’t get the dependent demand in the planning
and scheduling system and scheduling (as the S1 planned order isn’t available in the
planning and scheduling system and scheduling), and material C1 is left unplanned.
In addition, when scheduling MRP runs in the ERP systems and the PP/DS planning
runs in the planning and scheduling system, provide enough time gap between the
completion of the PP/DS planning run before starting the MRP planning runs in the
ERP systems. If the queues generated for the planned orders and purchase requisitions,

9.5 Summary
In this chapter, we covered the application and technical architecture of SAP Digital
Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA’s main solution for our area of
focus, SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling. We covered the steps
to set up the integration of the ERP systems to the SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for
planning and scheduling system and also the data flow for master data and transaction
data. SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling can help companies
with long-term plans for migrating to SAP S/4HANA from SAP ERP core systems to
leverage the PP/DS capabilities in SAP S/4HANA in a sidecar fashion. In addition, for
companies that want to leverage the latest improvements and innovations in PP/DS,
SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling can aid them with frequent
upgrades and keep the core ERP system to maintain its own upgrade cycles.
In the next chapter, we’ll cover the details on administrating the embedded PP/DS sys-
tem.
